# Junglizer

> Junglizer is a four-bar break instrument plugin for macOS, Windows and Linux. You chop four breaks (the built-in amen or your own), arrange the slices into an editable 16-beat jungle phrase, and play it in time with your DAW. It ships as AUv2 (Logic Pro, GarageBand), VST3 (Ableton Live, Cubase, Studio One) and CLAP (Bitwig, Reaper) for Apple Silicon and Intel Macs, plus VST3 and CLAP for Windows x86_64 and Linux x86_64. Version 0.9.2 beta 3 is free.

Junglizer is made by Todd Greco (mrballistic). Junglizer’s own 174 BPM amen ships inside the plugin, so there is nothing else to install. You can load your own WAV, AIFF or MP3 breaks (4 to 32 beats, 80 to 195 BPM, tempo read from the filename when present) into four slots; KAN Samples’ free Amen Break Tribute and Think Break Tribute packs are one source, downloaded from KAN separately and not bundled. The plugin follows the host’s tempo; away from a break’s own tempo the breaks change speed and pitch to stay on the grid. It makes no network connections and collects no data. The macOS builds are signed and notarized by Apple; the Windows and Linux builds are unsigned, and Linux is beta.

## Features

- Load up to four breaks of your own, with Relink for moved files and half/double tempo correction.
- Slice each source break into 1 to 32 slices (a separate count per break), drag markers onto the hits, audition, mute and tag bass hits.
- Pick a different break for each of the four bars; until slices are placed, the full break plays underneath as a ghost.
- Place slices on the player grid with per-slice length, Original or Fit speed, bit depth, retriggers (up to 8×) and locks.
- Fill and lock on each bar header, with Undo (Cmd/Ctrl+Z) for Fill and Remove; a Mode control (Edit, Live, Frozen) for a new phrase every four bars or keeping the one you like.
- One crossfader from Thin (high-passed) through Dry to Thicc, which layers a decaying 808 on tagged bass hits, down to a sub octave.
- Export the phrase as a four-bar MIDI file (slice notes, bar sources and controller data) to Junglizer/Exports in your operating system’s Music folder.
- Every control is a host automation parameter; phrases, markers, placements and locks are saved with the project.
